images.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a meticulously art-directed 16:9 editorial cover for a developer article about Vietnamese accent-insensitive search running locally in the browser. One oversized browser search panel occupies the central 80 percent. In its search input show EXACT lowercase text 'bao mat' beside a large recognizable magnifying glass and small insertion cursor. The original accented result is retained; give the result a broad coral highlight behind the words and a blue check at right. Two narrower unselected cards behind it contain only abstract horizontal line shapes, no words. A small elegant keyboard enter key in the lower-right of the search panel conveys choosing the result. Large memorable hierarchy, confident asymmetric framing, polished editorial finish; no big article title, logos, watermark, glassmorphism, neon, ornamental code, brains or robots. images.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a striking 16:9 technical editorial cover explaining that an application can be alive but unable to serve useful requests. Style: refined high-contrast dark charcoal technical cutaway, controlled matte materials, precise white linework, emerald green for the live process and vermilion red for failed readiness. NOT the common navy cyan amber glass-server aesthetic. Center-left one large application process enclosure, internally an elegant continuous green pulse loop shows its worker is still running. Attach two very large clean status tabs to this same enclosure: top tab EXACT 'LIVE' with a green circular check; lower tab EXACT 'READY' with a red square cross. Center-right one clearly identifiable large database cylinder. A single necessary application-to-database connection runs horizontally from enclosure to database and has a visible gap interrupted by a large red X. The database is dim, with a small red failure indicator. One incoming white request path from left stops at a closed red traffic gate just before entering the application; use a simple request-card shape to show it cannot be admitted while the process remains alive. This is one app and one database, no extra servers or alternate healthy pods, no restart arrows, no pulse on database, no imaginary repair. The live pulse must be visibly independent of the failed DB path. Allowed exact text only 'LIVE', 'READY', 'DB' (DB on database). Big tangible forms, intelligent hierarchy and intentional fine detail, not an infographic poster. No heading, prose, tiny labels, decorative shields, logos or watermark. Compose with 7 percent safe margins; LIVE/READY, failed connection and active process read clearly at 320x180.

images.name: 04-forward-proxy-va-reverse-proxy
images.message: The defining difference is whether the proxy represents clients or the service.
coverage: Proxy forwards request/response; software may support both roles.
Forward proxy owned/configured by client side; hides client's source IP.
CONNECT tunnels TLS ordinarily; corporate root certificate enables interception.
VPN network tunnel differs from application proxy; DNS/firewall blocking not proof of proxy.
Reverse proxy belongs to service; single front door, routing, TLS, cache and balancing.
Nginx forwards Host and original IP/protocol headers to upstream pool.
Express trust proxy must match controlled topology; blanket trust permits spoofed header issues.
Comparison table ownership, visibility and client awareness; check live app configuration.
concepts: Side-by-side ownership boundaries with consistent request direction.
Two architectural gatehouse metaphors representing a client office and service campus.
images.choice: Ownership boundaries drawn as distinct architectural floorplans; visual grouping conveys meaning even before labels.
caveats: Requests flow toward origin in both cases; reverse is not reversed arrow direction.
Do not imply all proxies decrypt TLS or proxy equals VPN.
Do not use forged IP or trust settings in decorative labels.
images.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished landscape 16:9 editorial network architecture illustration, two carefully balanced side-by-side scenes with no connecting path between scenes. Graphic style: precise axonometric architectural model on warm cream paper with fine engraved contour lines, subtle cast shadows, cobalt client objects and rich terracotta service objects, sophisticated clean print design. LEFT scene heading exactly 'FORWARD PROXY'. A clearly visible blue-outlined client-side platform contains two laptop clients and a gateway at the outgoing edge; gateway is inside this SAME platform. A large cobalt arrow leaves laptops through that gateway, crosses open neutral space, reaches a separate terracotta origin server OUTSIDE the platform. RIGHT scene heading exactly 'REVERSE PROXY'. One cobalt laptop OUTSIDE the service platform sends a large arrow rightward across neutral space to a gateway on the entrance of a terracotta-outlined service platform; gateway and two terracotta origin servers are all inside this SAME platform. The gateway splits the received path to the two origin servers within the service platform. In BOTH scenes requests move from clients toward servers, left to right. Ownership shown by visibly raised bases with complete enclosing borders, not by different arrow direction. Depict laptops and servers with distinctive silhouettes and gateways as clean vertical archways, not shield icons or cloned generic boxes. Only two headings, no other text, letters, numbers or subtitles. Important: left grouping is clients plus proxy; right grouping is proxy plus origins. Keep ample separation and hierarchy; technical meaning must remain visible with headings covered. Refined detailed models yet bold at 320x180. No glow, translucent glass, branded logos, watermark, or tiny UI panels. Safe margins 6 percent.

images.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create an exceptional 16:9 editorial magazine illustration about investigating bot traffic and spam backlinks before taking drastic action. Use a distinctive sophisticated cut-paper / screenprint collage aesthetic: deep aubergine desk background, warm off-white paper, coral traffic marks and acid-lime inspection accents; tactile paper grain, crisp deliberate geometry, subtle layered shadows, no generic cyber glow. Main focal point is one oversized magnifying glass in the foreground centered over the seam between two large evidence cards on a desk. LEFT evidence card has exact short heading 'TRAFFIC': a clear coral time-series with one abnormally tall spike, beside a neat group of repeated small request rectangles; two distinct legitimate rounded user tokens remain visible among those rectangles, so it is not a claim all traffic is malicious. RIGHT evidence card has exact short heading 'BACKLINKS': a simple network of several small page silhouettes with chain-link marks pointing toward one larger website page; a few suspicious links are coral while a few normal links remain neutral. Under magnifying glass the relevant request and chain details are larger and sharper, emphasizing examining evidence, not automatic removal. A small plain browser-shaped central website silhouette quietly connects the meaning of the two evidence cards; it is not burning, broken or labeled penalized. Differentiate a graph of request volume from a network of linking pages visually. No shields, giant padlocks, hooded hackers, robots, flags, giant red delete buttons, falling ranking arrows, guaranteed penalty or instant repair. Only exact text 'TRAFFIC' and 'BACKLINKS', no invented dashboard numbers or sentences. Confident composition, rich crafted editorial detail, one strong focal action readable at thumbnail 320x180; keep essential content inside 7 percent safe margins.
